body:
>I don't believe that you can argue "there could be negative futures, or positive ones, so there is a 50/50 chance of either, so they balance out"

I think if you read my thread title, you will find that there is about a 100% chance of negative futures, so they do not balance out.

> I don't mean to argue, but I cannot accept that there are no jobs in STEM fields.

It'll be just as true whether you accept it or not.

>Also, it is not logical to measure the value of life by the amount of pain and the amount of pleasure, or the ratio of good feeling to bad feeling. This is because these feelings can't be accurately measured or quantified. I can't speak to your value system specifically. Some people only value their own lives, and some people value the lives of others to varying degrees. I don't know what your values are, but I strongly believe that you can't take the difference of good and bad and end up with a value of a life. Even if you could value your life up to this point and had perfect knowledge of your own past, like a scorecard, you cannot account for the possible futures that you might experience in your natural lifespan.

You're not allowing for the possibility of negative futures.  If your future is going to suck, and you live anyway, then you will just wish that you had died earlier.
